direct_EMC_fusion_splicing.title: The EWS/NOR1 fusion gene product gains a novel activity affecting pre-mRNA splicing.
direct_EMC_fusion_splicing.source_level: Primary abstract only; not full methods/results inspected
direct_EMC_fusion_splicing.relevant_abstract: In extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma, chromosomal translocation creates a gene fusion between EWS and the orphan nuclear receptor NOR1. The resulting fusion gene product, EWS/NOR1, has been believed to lead to malignant transformation by functioning as a transcriptional activator, but an alternative mechanism may also be involved. Here, using a newly developed functional complementation screening in yeast, we found that EWS/NOR1, but not EWS or NOR1, complemented the loss of function of the small nuclear ribonucleoprotein Snu23p, an essential factor for pre-mRNA splicing in yeast. To verify the potential function of EWS/NOR1 in mammalian cells, we next showed that overexpression of EWS/NOR1 caused increased usage of the distal 5'-splice site of pre-mRNA splicing and that EWS/NOR1 interacted with the human splicing protein U1C; neither EWS nor NOR1 had the same activity or interaction as EWS/NOR1. Altogether, our findings reveal that EWS/NOR1 gains a novel activity affecting pre-mRNA splicing.
direct_EMC_fusion_splicing.interpretation: Engineered EWS/NOR1(NR4A3) pre-mRNA splicing/U1C activity is already published. It is not a native EMC partner comparison or mature retained-intron measurement. A general fusion-splicing claim has no novelty; retained native RNA phenotype could be distinct.

native_TAF15_U1.observations: HeLa chromatin-associated TAF15/U1 complex is distinct from canonical Sm/U1 snRNP. RNA-dependent chromatin association and transcription-related localization were investigated. Authors propose splicing or transcription initiation functions; mature retained introns and EMC are not demonstrated.
